source.evidence_text:
US citizen Stephen Hubbard freed by Russia as Trump envoy meets Putin
The 74-year-old former teacher has been released without any "swap" required, Trump says.
Russia has released a 74-year-old American citizen who was jailed for allegedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine, as President Vladimir Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg for talks.
President Donald Trump later said the former teacher was "on his way back home" and "there was no 'swap' necessary".
Writing on social media after Russian state media reported the release, Trump said it had followed a request he "made directly" to Putin last week.
CBS News, the BBC's US media partner, reported that Hubbard had been in poor health and was expected to be flown to Texas for treatment.
Hubbard was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony in 2024. He was accused of serving in a defence unit in Izyum, Ukraine, when he was captured by Russian forces shortly after Moscow's full-scale invasion in 2022.
The US State Department had previously classified Hubbard, from Michigan, as "wrongfully detained" and the US president had suggested on Tuesday that his release may be imminent.
The US envoy, who had attended talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky in Norway the previous day, also asked Putin to consider renewing trilateral peace talks with Ukraine as the war grinds on in its fifth year.
Trump also appeared to defend his recent decision to suspend sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to come into force , writing that "if sanctions would have been placed", negotiations for Hubbard's release "would have come to a complete and total halt".
Stephen Hubbard has been taken to Pulkovo Airport, Putin said during the meeting early on Wednesday.
He thanked Putin for the deal struck with Washington earlier this month to import Russian diesel , saying Trump was "deeply grateful" for it.
The diesel deal infuriated Zelensky and triggered a tumultuous few weeks of deteriorating relations during which Trump suspended a number of sanctions and said it was time for Ukraine to elect a new leader.
Kyiv meanwhile accused Washington of halting intelligence sharing on deadly Russian strikes , causing Ukrainians to lose their lives - an allegation Washington rejected as "scandalous" - and claimed a sudden restriction to the Starshield internet service in its war effort had been deliberate.
The Ukrainian president said on Tuesday that intelligence sharing had resumed, following talks with Witkoff in Oslo described by a US official as "constructive".

grammar.example_quote: Stephen Hubbard was sentenced to almost seven years in a penal colony after Russian forces captured him in 2022.
grammar.explanation: The past simple passive is formed using "was" or "were" plus the past participle of the main verb. It is used to focus on an action that happened to the subject, rather than who did the action. In the example sentence, "was sentenced" focuses on what happened to Stephen Hubbard, while the active verb "captured" focuses on what the Russian forces did.

grammar.example_quote: This diesel agreement infuriated Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, triggering a tumultuous period of deteriorating relations.
grammar.explanation: A present participle like "triggering" can introduce a phrase that describes the direct consequence of the action in the main clause. This structure offers a sophisticated way to link a cause to its immediate effect without starting a new sentence.

news_brief_sentences: Russia has released a 74-year-old American who was jailed for purportedly fighting on behalf of Ukraine.
The Russian president confirmed during an early Wednesday meeting that Stephen Hubbard had been transported to Pulkovo Airport.
Donald Trump stated that the release followed a direct request he made to the Russian leader last week.
He added that the release did not require any reciprocal concessions from the United States.
American news outlets reported that the elderly man was in poor health and expected to be flown to Texas for medical care.
Trump defended his move to pause impending sanctions against Russia, arguing that enforcing them would have brought diplomatic discussions to a complete halt.
Steve Witkoff thanked Putin for a deal struck with Washington earlier this month to import Russian diesel.
This diesel agreement infuriated Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, triggering a tumultuous period of deteriorating relations.
Witkoff also urged Putin to consider resuming trilateral peace talks, seeking an end to a conflict that grinds on into its fifth year.
Meanwhile, Kyiv accused Washington of withholding vital intelligence, a claim the US firmly rejected as scandalous.
However, Zelensky confirmed that intelligence sharing had resumed after constructive talks with American officials in Oslo.
